documents.title: Faculty Resources (Artificial Intelligence at UNF)
tiers: Suggested syllabus language ranging from incorporating generative AI into coursework to prohibiting its use (text on UNF intranet, not shown)
documents.summary: Faculty-facing page that tells instructors to set clear boundaries in their syllabi, points to suggested syllabus wording on the intranet, and lists ways to redesign or limit AI in assignments. It also covers faculty training, Copilot as the official tool, and tips and caveats on spotting AI text.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI rule for students itself: it says "Students will use AI, so set clear and upfront boundaries on its allowed and prohibited uses" and offers syllabus language "ranging from incorporating generative AI into coursework to prohibiting its use", so the decision is left to instructors (delegates).

units.why: The page offers instructors ready-made syllabus wording, "ranging from incorporating generative AI into coursework to prohibiting its use"; supplying templates is P110, and it is addressed to the university side (admin) as a resource, so informs/neutral.
units.anchor: ranging from incorporating generative AI into coursework to prohibiting its use

units.why: "set clear and upfront boundaries on its allowed and prohibited uses" tells instructors to put AI limits in place before students start, so it is P09 (state expectations), instructor, course-start, should.
units.anchor: set clear and upfront boundaries on its allowed and prohibited uses

units.why: Instructors are pointed to the suggested wording "to outline the expected use of AI in the course"; the thing recommended is adopting template language, so P110 rather than P09 (covered by the previous unit).
units.anchor: Explore the suggested syllabus language to outline the expected use of AI in the course.

units.why: "Be transparent and address the topic upfront with students" asks instructors to talk about AI with students at the start; this is explaining/discussing rules (P66), not a syllabus requirement.
units.anchor: Be transparent and address the topic upfront with students.

units.why: "be explicit about your expectations and the consequences that will follow" tells instructors to say in advance how prohibited AI use will be handled, which is P123; no concrete penalty is named so P37 does not fit.
units.anchor: be explicit about your expectations and the consequences that will follow
units.fit_note: Asks for explicit expectations and consequences when AI is not tolerated, not specifically how misuse is detected.

units.why: "Educate your students on the benefits and limitations of AI" is an instruction to teach AI literacy to students, matching P70 (curricular AI literacy).
units.anchor: Educate your students on the benefits and limitations of AI.
units.fit_note: Instructor-delivered teaching of AI benefits and limits rather than an institutional training program.

units.why: "Mentor them on how to use AI securely and responsibly" asks instructors to guide students on safe use; closest is P70 but it also touches secure use of data, so a fit note records the gap.
units.anchor: Mentor them on how to use AI securely and responsibly.
units.fit_note: Mentoring on secure and responsible use, not a formal training or module.

units.why: "Create an introductory assignment to help students explore the platform and provide effective prompts" asks for a prompt-writing exercise; closest type is P93 (advice on prompting), but it is delivered as an assignment.
units.anchor: Create an introductory assignment to help students explore the platform
units.fit_note: Recommends an introductory assignment for students to explore the AI platform and practice prompts.

units.why: "UNF highly recommends that students begin with digital badge courses" is a recommendation of AI training to students, matching P70 (students are offered AI-literacy courses).
units.anchor: UNF highly recommends that students begin with digital badge courses.

units.why: "Redesign assignments to account for the potential use of AI" directly tells instructors to change assignments because of AI: P35.
units.anchor: Redesign assignments to account for the potential use of AI.

units.why: "Consider how AI can be thoughtfully integrated into activities or deterred" leaves to each instructor whether to integrate or deter AI, so P04 (instructor sets the rule).
units.anchor: Consider how AI can be thoughtfully integrated into activities or deterred.

units.why: "Develop creative assignments that require personal reflection" is one of three listed redesign moves in response to AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Develop creative assignments that require personal reflection.

units.why: "Develop critical-thinking assignments that reveal students' thought processes" is a second redesign move; assigning work that exposes thinking fits P35.
units.anchor: Develop critical-thinking assignments that reveal students' thought processes.

units.why: "Develop analytical assignments that require deeper investigation" is a third redesign move in response to AI, P35.
units.anchor: Develop analytical assignments that require deeper investigation.

units.why: "Encourage face-to-face interaction in the classroom without the use of devices" moves learning into unassisted, in-person settings, closest to P33.
units.anchor: Encourage face-to-face interaction in the classroom without the use of devices.
units.fit_note: Device-free classroom interaction generally, not specifically weighted assessment.

units.why: The passage says the human side matters: "value creativity, empathy, and the unique perspectives that only human experiences can bring" and balancing AI benefits with personal experience. This is a rationale for redesign that fits no type (P41 is about skill practice).
units.anchor: value creativity, empathy, and the unique perspectives that only human experiences can bring
units.uncovered_note: Rationale that human creativity, empathy and lived perspective should be valued and balanced against AI's benefits.

units.why: "Microsoft Copilot is the official generative AI tool available to all UNF faculty, students, and staff" names the institution-wide sanctioned tool, so P92 (university-licensed tool, not course-specific).
units.anchor: Microsoft Copilot is the official generative AI tool available to all UNF faculty

units.why: "Generative AI can help you ideate and customize interactive activities" says instructors may use AI to prepare classroom activities: P59 (instructor AI use for teaching work).
units.anchor: Generative AI can help you ideate and customize interactive activities

units.why: Under "How can I limit the use of AI?" the page lists "Oral Exams or Presentations", where students explain their work, so P34.
units.anchor: Oral Exams or Presentations

units.why: "In-Class Writing" is listed as a way to limit AI use; it moves evaluation into supervised, unassisted settings (P33).
units.anchor: In-Class Writing

units.why: "Monitor progress through drafts, mockups, and prototypes" uses process evidence to check student work, matching P40 (process evidence instead of detection).
units.anchor: Monitor progress through drafts, mockups, and prototypes
units.fit_note: Drafts and prototypes as monitoring of progress, not explicitly framed as misuse detection.

units.why: "set clear expectations with your students on how AI may or may not be used in assignments" asks instructors to state per-assignment rules, so P09.
units.anchor: set clear expectations with your students on how AI may or may not be used

units.why: "Familiarize yourself with these resources" points instructors to the AI-detection, integrity and misconduct policy pages, so P115.
units.anchor: Familiarize yourself with these resources

units.why: "increasingly difficult to distinguish between human-generated and AI-generated content" admits limits on verifying authorship, matching P82.
units.anchor: it's becoming increasingly difficult to distinguish between human-generated and AI-generated content

units.why: "Here are some tips and tools for identifying AI-generated text" gives instructors signs (inconsistency, lack of depth, poor grammar, failed fact-check) for spotting AI work, i.e. P40 for identifying misuse by checks.
units.anchor: Here are some tips and tools for identifying AI-generated text
units.fit_note: Content-based clues (inconsistency, shallow content, odd phrasing, unchecked facts) rather than software or process logs.

units.why: "third-party reviews have revealed higher rates of false positives" and OpenAI "could not reliably detect" its software: the passage says detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: third-party reviews have revealed higher rates of false positives

units.why: "Exclusively for UNF Faculty CIRT offers two valuable badges" on AI for teaching gives faculty training on AI, matching P63.
units.anchor: Exclusively for UNF Faculty CIRT offers two valuable badges.

units.why: "provides guidance and workshops on integrating AI into the classroom" describes faculty support from the Office of Faculty Enhancement: P63.
units.anchor: provides guidance and workshops on integrating AI into the classroom

units.why: The Faculty Information Hub is "a central resource for understanding and exploring AI in teaching and research", a faculty support resource, P63.
units.anchor: A central resource for understanding and exploring AI in teaching and research.

units.why: "UNF faculty are encouraged to seek grants and support for developing impactful research about AI" is an institutional encouragement of AI research, P122 (not a use rule).
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to seek grants and support for developing impactful research about AI

units.why: "The Innovation in AI Grants aim to advance the use of Artificial Intelligence to enhance teaching, student success" is institutional funding for AI in teaching, P122.
units.anchor: The Innovation in AI Grants aim to advance the use of Artificial Intelligence

documents.title: UNF AI guidelines
documents.summary: University AI guidelines page giving five guiding principles and a table showing how AI bears on existing UNF policies. Its main student-facing rules are that AI may be used for coursework only when the syllabus or assignment authorizes it, that authorized use is cited, and that AI-generated work submitted as one's own is misconduct; it also recommends against AI detectors.
documents.stance_why: The one binding rule on coursework in the table is "AI may only be used to complete coursework when authorized via the course syllabus or specific assignment instructions", which is a ban unless permitted (restrict); the rest of the page is principles and policy implications that do not change that default.

units.why: "the UNF AI Council will guide recommendations for the ethical and safe integration of AI" names the body that owns AI guidance, P80.
units.anchor: UNF AI Council will guide recommendations for the ethical and safe integration of AI technologies

units.why: "Artificial intelligence tools will augment learning and research in ethical ways" is a framing statement of purpose for the policy, P56.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence tools will augment learning and research in ethical ways.

units.why: "UNF recommends not using these tools for academic assignments unless they become significantly more reliable and transparent" says not to use AI detectors, P39 (should-not, a recommendation).
units.anchor: recommends not using these tools for academic assignments unless they become significantly more reliable

units.why: "UNF offers access to approved technologies and helpful tutorials" tells the community which vetted tools exist, P92.
units.anchor: UNF offers access to approved technologies and helpful tutorials

units.why: "mastering the art of writing effective AI prompts can significantly enhance your AI experience" is prompting advice, P93.
units.anchor: mastering the art of writing effective AI prompts can significantly enhance your AI experience

units.why: "The University of North Florida establishes the following guiding principles for the use of Artificial Intelligence" sets an institution-wide framework, P56.
units.anchor: establishes the following guiding principles for the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: "These principles will be further codified and articulated in relevant policy documents" says the principles are a stage that will be developed, a provisional status; closest is P54.
units.anchor: These principles will be further codified and articulated in relevant policy documents
units.fit_note: States the principles will be codified in later policy documents, not periodic review.

units.why: "These principles will also guide how we work with AI and our partners in the northeast Florida region" extends AI principles to external partnerships, P88.
units.anchor: guide how we work with AI and our partners in the northeast Florida region

units.why: "AI is a tool and as such has its uses, strengths, limitations and risks" asks users to understand AI as a tool with limits and risks. It does not require verification, so P31 is wrong; nearest is P118 (weighing benefits and risks).
units.anchor: AI is a tool and as such has its uses, strengths, limitations and risks.
units.fit_note: Asks users to understand AI as a tool with strengths and risks; no instruction to weigh before use.

units.why: "communicating when and how they used such tools in their work products and class projects" requires disclosure of AI use, P24.
units.anchor: communicating when and how they used such tools in their work products and class projects

units.why: "use AI tools in ethical ways that do not compromise intellectual property rights, data privacy, or our academic rigor and honor" is a general expectation of ethical use, P116, though it names IP and privacy.
units.anchor: use AI tools in ethical ways that do not compromise intellectual property rights, data privacy
units.fit_note: Names intellectual property, data privacy and academic honor as the limits on ethical use.

units.why: "use AI to enhance and add value to our intellectual and creative work, our teaching and learning and our operations" welcomes AI use as a value, P02.
units.anchor: use AI to enhance and add value to our intellectual and creative work

units.why: "promote a culture of care where the study and use of AI will center the importance and value of humans in all their diversity, and enable participation by all members" speaks to inclusion, nearest P51.
units.anchor: enable participation by all members of our community
units.fit_note: Principle of inclusion and a culture of care, not specifically cost or access to tools.

units.why: Under Disruptive Behavior: "AI can create misinformation, disrupting University processes" flags misinformation as a conduct concern, P74.
units.anchor: AI can create misinformation, disrupting University processes.

units.why: "AI can generate fake scholarly content or tools that potentially undermine academics" names fabricated scholarly content as a disruption, P74.
units.anchor: AI can generate fake scholarly content or tools that potentially undermine academics.

units.why: "AI can access or manipulate University systems without permission" is a conduct warning on unauthorized system access, P74.
units.anchor: AI can access or manipulate University systems without permission.

units.why: "AI can automate actions that programmatically disrupt University functions" warns against disruptive automation, P74.
units.anchor: AI can automate actions that programmatically disrupt University functions.

units.why: "AI systems in grading or admissions should be transparent and unbiased" sets expectations for institutional AI systems; closest is P98 (monitoring for bias).
units.anchor: AI systems in grading or admissions should be transparent and unbiased.
units.fit_note: Asks that systems used in grading or admissions be transparent and unbiased, without mention of audits or documentation.

units.why: "avoiding plagiarism and acknowledging AI contributions to maintain academic integrity" requires acknowledgment of AI contributions, P24.
units.anchor: avoiding plagiarism and acknowledging AI contributions to maintain academic integrity

units.why: "AI systems should be free from bias and prevent discrimination based on race, sex or disability" is an ethics rule on bias, P53.
units.anchor: AI systems should be free from bias and prevent discrimination based on race

units.why: "Maintain confidentiality and security of university information. By using university approved tools" protects data and points to approved tools, P50.
units.anchor: Maintain confidentiality and security of university information.

units.why: "AI systems must be financially transparent and prevent misuse" is a financial transparency rule on AI systems that matches no type.
units.anchor: AI systems must be financially transparent and prevent misuse.
units.uncovered_note: AI systems must be financially transparent and prevent misuse (proper use of resources).

units.why: "AI use in decision-making or data analysis should be transparent and auditable to comply with public record laws" requires auditability and legal compliance; nearest is P98 (audit/monitor).
units.anchor: transparent and auditable to comply with public record laws
units.fit_note: Ties auditability to compliance with public record laws.

units.why: "provide mechanisms for reporting and addressing AI-related ethical violations" requires a channel to report AI violations, P71.
units.anchor: provide mechanisms for reporting and addressing AI-related ethical violations.

units.why: "AI applications should support a climate of care and civility, avoiding biased or hostile environments" is an ethics expectation on harms, P53.
units.anchor: AI applications should support a climate of care and civility, avoiding biased or hostile environments.

units.why: "AI may only be used to complete coursework when authorized via the course syllabus or specific assignment instructions" sets a default ban unless authorized, which is the fallback rule P06 (and the document stance restrict).
units.anchor: AI may only be used to complete coursework when authorized via the course syllabus

units.why: "Authorized use of AI should be appropriately cited in coursework" requires citation of permitted AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Authorized use of AI should be appropriately cited in coursework.

units.why: "Use of AI to cyberbully, harass, stalk or do harm" is listed under the Student Code of Conduct as misconduct, P74.
units.anchor: Use of AI to cyberbully, harass, stalk or do harm.

units.why: "AI should not be used to generate work for academic credit that is not the student's own" forbids having AI produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: AI should not be used to generate work for academic credit

units.why: "Unauthorized assistance can include work generated by AI" classifies AI-generated work as unauthorized assistance under conduct rules, P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized assistance can include work generated by AI.

units.why: "AI-generated content used without proper attribution" is classed as plagiarism, P36.
units.anchor: AI-generated content used without proper attribution.

units.why: "sharing instructor-created materials without permission" is named as misuse of materials; it restricts passing course materials on, closest P49.
units.anchor: sharing instructor-created materials without permission
units.fit_note: Covers sharing instructor materials without permission and AI-generated content as course materials; does not mention uploading to AI tools.

units.why: "a student's right to allow the presentation of evidence in AI misconduct cases" gives students a right to respond, P64.
units.anchor: right to allow the presentation of evidence in AI misconduct cases

units.why: "Apply existing sanctions, including forfeiture of academic credit, to cases of AI misconduct" states that existing penalties apply; nearest P37 (forfeiture of credit) though no specific sanction schedule is given.
units.anchor: Apply existing sanctions, including forfeiture of academic credit, to cases of AI misconduct.
units.fit_note: Applies existing sanctions, naming forfeiture of academic credit, rather than a list of penalties by offense.

units.why: "Specify the weight of AI-generated grades compared to an instructor’s judgment and clarify how instructors can contest or override AI decisions" preserves instructor authority over AI grades, closest P46.
units.anchor: clarify how instructors can contest or override AI decisions
units.fit_note: Does not ban AI grades; asks to define their weight against instructor judgment and a way to override.

units.why: "Ensure the committee has expertise in evaluating AI grading methodologies" adds a requirement on the grade-appeal committee that fits no type.
units.anchor: Ensure the committee has expertise in evaluating AI grading methodologies.
units.uncovered_note: Grade-appeals committees should have expertise in evaluating AI grading methods.

units.why: "Update the curriculum to include AI-related courses or integrate AI concepts into existing courses" commits to curricular AI literacy, P70.
units.anchor: Update the curriculum to include AI-related courses or integrate AI concepts into existing courses
units.fit_note: Curriculum change for certificate programs, not a student training module.

units.why: "Define new learning outcomes related to AI competencies and evolve assessment methods" ties AI competence to outcomes and assessment; P83 is about AI rules, so nearest is P70.
units.anchor: Define new learning outcomes related to AI competencies
units.fit_note: Defines AI competency learning outcomes and assessment methods for certificates.

units.why: "Develop new certificate programs in AI-related areas like Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning or Data Science" is an institutional investment in AI programs, P122.
units.anchor: Develop new certificate programs in AI-related areas

units.why: "Explicitly include AI-related terms in definitions of Invention and Work" asks policy definitions to cover AI, P61.
units.anchor: Explicitly include AI-related terms in definitions of

units.why: "Ownership of AI-generated content" is listed as an IP challenge to address, P52.
units.anchor: Ownership of AI-generated content.

units.why: "Ownership of data sets used to train AI models" is a listed IP challenge, P52.
units.anchor: Ownership of data sets used to train AI models.

units.why: "Ethical implications of AI development and deployment" is listed as an issue to address, P53.
units.anchor: Ethical implications of AI development and deployment.

units.why: "Consider changes related to AI in the context of existing collective bargaining agreements with faculty" requires staying within existing agreements, P77.
units.anchor: existing collective bargaining agreements with faculty

units.why: "Syllabi will include a statement about acceptable use of AI in the course" requires an AI statement in every syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: Syllabi will include a statement about

notes: Many table rows in the guidelines page are described as what policies 'should' address (policy implications), so modality is mostly should. Program-administration rows (eligibility, transfer credit, residency, good standing, conferral on transcripts) were not coded as they are not about AI use rules. Faculty page's syllabus language is behind the intranet and not seen.
